entries: Input confirmation | Read the casting drawing | Mark key dimensions, parting, materials, shrinkage, and machining allowances, and record conditions still awaiting confirmation by the process owner.
Layout planning | Mark and segment the lumber per the approved drawing | Record datums, measuring tools, and machining sequence, and do not treat undetermined tolerances as approved.
Machining and forming | Cut and shape the lumber | Equipment guards, training, and protection follow workplace rules.

Assembly and fitting | Join pattern sections with glue, nails, pins, or fasteners | Check location, joints, and parting surfaces during trial assembly, and confirm that section breakdown meets later sand molding and draft requirements.

Dimension verification | Check the pattern with templates, straightedges, calipers, or angle gauges | Record measurement points, actual values, drawing version, and out-of-tolerance handling against the specified datums, and re-measure after rework.

Identification and handoff | Mark patterns or components with identifying information and keep rework records | Verify pattern version, delivery scope, and open issues with foundry, process, or quality staff.

paragraphs:
Task object | Building wooden sand-casting patterns to casting drawings.
Work setting | In the patternmaking area and woodworking equipment area designated by the employer, laying out, cutting, assembling, measuring, and shaping to drawing requirements, then handing off to molding, foundry, or quality operations. Workshop layout, shifts, equipment use scope, and supervision must be verified with the specific employer, and the job title alone does not guarantee the same environment. On entry, also confirm dust collection, protection, and handoff locations.

Equipment and tools | Select straightedges, calipers, templates, hand tools, and woodworking machinery for which the operator has received training per the work requirement; specific models, fixturing, guards, and measuring tool calibration are set by the plant. CAD/CAM can assist design and records, but a digital model does not automatically prove that physical dimensions conform.

Dimensional precision requirements | Use the approved drawing and process documents as the basis, and verify datums, key dimensions, tolerances, shrinkage, and machining allowances; re-check location and parting surfaces during section trial assembly. If drawing conditions are missing or measurements are out of tolerance, pause the affected steps and hand them to the process or quality owner.

Personal protection | Use the required eye, hearing, dust, or other protection based on the on-site risk assessment for cutting, sanding, and finishing lumber; if dust collection, machine guards, or cleaning procedures fail, stop the machine and report per employer rules. US OSHA material is used for hazard identification and does not directly state Chinese post obligations.

Collaboration and handoff counterparts | Wood patternmakers confirm drawings and allowances with design or process staff, confirm parting, location, and usage issues with molding staff, and communicate measurement deviations and rework results with quality staff. Who holds change, release, or stop-work authority must be clear in the on-site responsibility chain.

Records and handoff | Keep drawing and pattern versions, key measurement points, actual values, rework locations, and open issues; verify that the current pattern identification matches the records before handoff, so old versions are not reissued downstream.

Main work risks | Woodworking machine cutters, flying chips, wood dust, noise, and handling and finishing materials carry different risks; these hazards must be controlled through on-site equipment guarding, dust collection, training, and work procedures. Specific controls are set by workplace rules and the employer's assessment.

Authority and responsibility boundaries | Wood patternmakers may record and report drawing gaps, dimension deviations, equipment faults, and rework results; process condition approval, independent operation of hazardous equipment, and final inspection release must follow local rules and employer authorization. US O*NET and OSHA material does not directly define Chinese post permits.

entries.answer: Wood patternmakers read casting drawings, confirm pattern dimensions and machining conditions, lay out and machine sections in lumber, and after assembly, shaping, and measurement deliver wooden patterns for sand casting; they rework defects and keep pattern records. The specific equipment and process are determined by the employer.
entries.question: What do wood patternmakers do every day?

entries.answer: Wood patternmakers make wooden patterns for sand casting; wood model makers may make full-size or scale product models. Both may read drawings, cut, and measure lumber, but the final use, process, and accepting party differ.
entries.question: How do wood patternmakers differ from wood model makers?

entries.answer: Start with a fictional casting drawing and a no-machine exercise: list dimensions, sections, measuring tools, tolerances that are not given, and safety conditions; then observe whether you are willing to shape, measure, and record repeatedly. entries.answer: High-risk points include misreading drawing versions or dimension datums, unconfirmed sections and draft conditions, inadequate woodworking machine guarding, exposure to flying chips and wood dust, and unrecorded pattern out-of-tolerance results. When equipment guards fail or key dimensions are unclear, pause the affected steps and hand them to authorized personnel.
